title: Charlie Chaplin and silent cinema
subject: art
description: **Charlie Chaplin** invents Charlot, a vagabond in a bowler hat, and becomes the first world cinema star. From silent to talking, he transforms laughter into art.

hero.hook: Before radio and TV, a mute wanderer made the entire planet laugh.

blocks.text: **Charlie Chaplin** (1889-1977) is the first true global celebrity. In an era of industrial poverty, his character **Charlotte**, a dignified and clumsy vagabond, offers a face of humanity. Without speaking, he makes people laugh and cry in Tokyo, Paris or New York.
This course follows his trajectory: from the origins of cinema to silent masterpieces, then to forced exile. Chaplin is not just a clown. He is a total author.

Cinema was born from a French invention: the [[Cinematograph]] of, patented in **1895**. **December 28, 1895**, at the Grand Café de Paris, the first paid public screening took place. The first films are short documents: a factory exit, a train at a station. [[The Lumière brothers and early cinema]]

blocks.caption: 1895: cinema becomes a collective spectacle in Paris.

blocks.text: Very quickly, , a French illusionist, invented fiction and tricks. Then the industry is structured in the United States. **Hollywood** becomes the capital of dreams, with its studios producing films on an assembly line. It is in this factory that Chaplin will establish himself. [[Georges Méliès]]

Born into poverty in London in **1889**, Charles Spencer Chaplin grew up between cabarets and homes for the poor. Trained at , he arrived in Hollywood. In **1914**, he almost accidentally invented the costume of **Charlotte**: bowler hat too small, pants too wide, cane and mustache. [[music-hall]]

blocks.caption: Charlot: a penniless gentleman, recognizable in a silhouette.

blocks.text: Chaplin put together the costume in a few minutes in a studio dressing room, borrowing clothes that were too big and too small from the other actors.
Charlot is not only funny. He symbolizes the man who clings to his dignity despite poverty. Chaplin uses , the comedy of falls and blows, but he adds a rare emotion: tenderness. [[Slapstick]]

In **1927**, sound cinema arrives with *The Jazz Singer*. Chaplin, co-founder of , resists. To give Charlot a voice is to break his universality. He therefore continues on silent with *City Lights* (**1931**). [[United Artists]]

Then history catches up with him. In **1940**, he directed *The Dictator*, a satire of **Adolf Hitler**. It is his first fully talking film, shot while the United States was still wary of Nazism. The clown becomes a committed artist.

sections.title: The exile and legacy of an author

blocks.text: After 1945, the [[Cold War]] and the [[McCarthyism]] were established. Suspected of left-wing ideas, Chaplin is monitored. In **1952**, when he left for Europe, the United States prohibited him from returning. He settled in, Switzerland, for the rest of his life. [[Vevey]]

events.title: Forced exile
events.detail: Banned from staying in the United States, he left for Switzerland.

blocks.text: Chaplin invented a universal silent language. A complete author (actor, director, composer), he proved that popular cinema could also be a political and emotional art.
